# Analysis Model

## Implemented formula-analysis contract

The independently importable `py-science-formula` distribution and readiness-gated Pi `analyze_formula` tool accept exactly one restricted-SymPy expression, one nonempty list of uniquely named `Eq` equations, or a separate candidate-comparison request containing exactly two such computations and explicit output mappings. Pi injects `syntax: sympy`; direct Python callers supply `FormulaSyntax.SYMPY`. Ordinary requests may attach equation output domains, variable domains, function definitions, scalar primitive costs, named assumptions, directed definitions, scenarios, and optional bounded general-context queries. Comparison requests share the mathematical metadata but omit scenarios and queries. Strict request validation rejects surplus fields and invalid computation unions.

Python owns request validation, restricted-expression parsing, and mathematical policy. A deterministic generator derives Pi's checked-in provider-compatible structural schema from `AnalysisRequest` and `CandidateComparisonRequest`, and the gate rejects drift. TypeScript imports that artifact, injects syntax, and carries the bounded protocol without recreating mathematical policy. Python request errors cross the bridge only through the exact bounded current-version request-error envelope; malformed, incompatible, wrong-status, surplus, or unbounded subprocess output fails closed.

The public Python boundary bounds request populations, aggregate source bytes and nodes, expression depth, integers, generated scenario results, rendering, and reports. Submitted formula, assumption, definition, query, and cost text is converted from restricted Python AST data only: it is never evaluated or passed to a SymPy string parser.

SymPy is the bounded backend for normalized algebra, rendering, and verification after project-owned syntax, family, and resource checks. Extend checked SymPy seams instead of recreating algebra when the backend already supplies the required mechanism. The typed internal model, work and reuse semantics, assumptions and provenance, supported-query policy, qualification, and fail-closed outcomes remain project-owned; unrestricted or unverified SymPy behavior never defines the public contract or constitutes proof.

## Restricted expression dialect

The parser accepts integer and exact decimal literals, ordinary symbols, `oo` and `-oo`, arithmetic `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, and `**`, indexed scalar values, bounded nonrecursive lexical bindings spelled `Let(name, value, body)`, and ordinary named calls with positional arguments. It accepts one-limit inclusive sums spelled `Sum(body, (index, lower, upper))`, equations spelled `Eq(lhs, rhs)` with a scalar or indexed result on the left, and one unchained `==`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=` relationship.

`Let` has one meaning: its bare-symbol name is not visible in `value`, is visible only in `body`, and `value` contributes work once per evaluation at that lexical placement. It is preserved in normalized syntax and lowered capture-safely only for represented-value mathematics; it is not a generic call, scheduling construct, mutation, or code generation feature.

The submitted language is not unrestricted Python or SymPy. It rejects attributes, keyword and starred call arguments, chained relationships, implicit vector operations, products, submitted aggregate `Max`, and multiple limits in one sum. An ordinary spelling such as `sqrt(x)`, `exp(x)`, or `f(x)` is a generic call unless the request supplies a function body or primitive cost; parser acceptance does not imply evaluator semantics. Parser acceptance, validity in the containing request field, and bounded query applicability are separate Python-owned checks.

## Expression and equation-system requests

Use `expression` for one self-contained formula:

```json
{
  "expression": "Sum((x[i] - center)**2, (i, 0, N - 1))",
  "variables": {
    "N": {"domain": "positive_integer"},
    "x": {"domain": "real"},
    "center": {"domain": "real"}
  }
}
```

Use named `equations` for reusable results with local output domains:

```json
{
  "equations": [
    {
      "name": "samples",
      "expression": "Eq(S[i], x[i] - center)",
      "domains": {"i": {"lower": "0", "upper": "N - 1"}}
    },
    {
      "name": "summary",
      "expression": "Eq(T[k], Sum(basis(S[i], k), (i, 0, N - 1)))",
      "domains": {"k": {"lower": "0", "upper": "p - 1"}}
    }
  ],
  "variables": {
    "N": {"domain": "positive_integer"},
    "p": {"domain": "positive_integer"},
    "x": {"domain": "real"},
    "center": {"domain": "real"}
  },
  "primitive_costs": [
    {"name": "basis", "parameters": ["value", "k"], "work": "k + 1"}
  ]
}
```

A free equation-output index needs a local domain. Output bounds may reference other output indices when their inferred graph is acyclic and every dependent bound is a finite sum of integer constants and integer multiples of declared integer variables or output indices. Calls, indexed values, symbolic products, powers, division, and aggregate operators are outside that dependent affine grammar; self-dependence and cycles are invalid. Existing independent bounds retain their accepted family. LHS order remains mathematical coordinate order and only breaks topological ties. A `Sum` iterator is local to its body. Every external symbol needs an intrinsic variable domain. A named equation is charged once per local output-domain point; downstream references are accesses to that result, while unnamed repetition remains submitted work. Output domains aggregate in reverse dependency order. Nested finite direct-work fields close bounded affine sums from intrinsic domains, supported substitutions and relationships, and predecessor-domain facts, or preserve each iterator under its lexical symbolic `Sum`, including operation counts, opaque work, and primitive invocations. Inclusive sums use proved nonnegative cardinality; unproved cardinality, ordering, or finiteness remains an explicit unresolved qualification rather than a free iterator. The reasoner and work closure retain their 4096-step/node budgets and do not broaden mathematical closed-form queries.

Use a function definition when a call's mathematical body is known, a primitive cost when its body is intentionally opaque but scalar work is known, or neither to retain an explicit unknown cost. Assumptions state named relationships. Directed definitions are acyclic substitutions. These inputs are explicit mathematical knowledge, not facts inferred by the analyzer.

## Scenarios and work reports

A scenario specializes the general report through fixed exact values, finite choices, finite bounds, directed definitions, or selected asymptotic variables. Exact values are JavaScript-safe JSON integers or exact strings such as `1/2` and `1.20`. Scenarios leave the general symbolic report unchanged and return substitutions, conservative supported intervals, bounded classifications, provenance, qualifications, and blockers.

Reports preserve normalized SymPy and LaTeX interpretations, symbolic operation and work counts, per-equation and total work, dependency edges and ideal reuse, repeated-expression extraction diagnostics, primitive invocations, used submitted and predecessor-domain relationship provenance, explicit unknown costs, and unresolved conclusions. Pi tool text is a compact human-readable projection organized around interpretation, closed forms or query conclusions, work, optimization advice, and blockers; for enabled advice it shows the first-ranked proved atomic transformation set, any intermediate, work savings, conditions, and finite-precision qualification, then names additional suggestions in the unchanged canonical report in `details`; deterministic presentation is not a superiority claim. It keeps incomplete-search guidance local to advice and remains quiet when advice is disabled. Inspect normalized interpretations before using a result. Then distinguish exact claims, claims under named assumptions, conservative bounds, conditional results, and unresolved quantities. A specialized scenario does not replace exact general work: `substituted_work` is specialized evaluation work, not represented mathematical value.

## Bounded optimization advice

Ordinary expression and equation-system analysis requests accept only `optimization.max_suggestions`. It defaults to 3, accepts strict integers from 0 through 16, and is an upper bound rather than a promised population; zero returns a disabled empty report. Candidate-comparison and dominance requests do not accept this setting. A completed empty report means the bounded search published no qualifying candidate. An incomplete report means an inspection, candidate, transformation, proof, work-comparison, or advice-output bound was reached; it may retain already proved suggestions and does not prove that no further improvement exists.

Python generates repeated-subexpression extraction, identical-call and reciprocal reuse, checked factoring, redundant-operation removal, iterator-invariant hoisting, compatible sharing across named equation RHSs, and bounded Horner reformulation. Shared producers require one positional free-index interface, compatible output domains, no equation-local constraint leakage, and acyclic insertion; they are charged once over that interface. Horner uses deterministic variable selection and explicit target-node, polynomial-variable, degree, term, and generated-node ceilings. Generated intermediates use collision-free names and the narrowest capture-safe lexical/output scope. Broader rewrite search, algorithm replacement, code generation, and target-specific optimization remain excluded.

Every family enters one verifier. It expands generated intermediates through checked substitution for semantic proof, verifies each retained output under declared domains and assumptions, and compares whole-computation aggregate abstract work including sum cardinality, output multiplicity, and intermediate evaluation scope. A suggestion publishes only when both work values are available and Python proves a positive reduction. Unknown primitive costs, unresolved cardinality or proof, incompatible scopes, capture risk, and nonpositive or incomparable savings are omitted. Unconditional suggestions precede assumption-dependent ones; deterministic ordering among incomparable savings is not a superiority claim.

Each suggestion contains a nonempty tuple of unique target-local transformations. Each transformation reports its expression or equation target, structural child-index paths, crossed binders and output indices, and normalized original and proposed forms; an optional generated intermediate and scope, exact identity evidence, denominator or assumption conditions, work before and after, savings, and `exact_symbolic_only` finite-precision qualification. Exact-symbolic reassociation does not claim identical floating-point evaluation or numerical stability. Advice never replaces or feeds submitted interpretation, operation counts, work, scenarios, dependencies, reuse, extraction diagnostics, or queries. Pi protocol v13 validates and transports the strict shape and request/result correlation but never recomputes algebra, work, applicability, ranking, or proof.

## Bounded mathematical queries

An optional `queries` collection remains separate from submitted work and scenarios. Each query has a unique name and one strict shape:

- `equivalence` supplies `comparison`;
- `closed_form` supplies no additional operand;
- `properties` supplies a nonempty unique list of `sign`, `valid_domain`, `singularities`, or `monotonicity` checks, with a variable where required;
- `limit` supplies a variable and exact point;
- `asymptotic` supplies the same point fields and an order from 1 through 8.

Finite points require `left`, `right`, or `both`; `oo` and `-oo` forbid direction. An expression query omits `target`. A system query selects one named equation RHS with `{ "kind": "equation", "name": "..." }`. An `equivalence` or `limit` may instead spell `{ "kind": "derived", "query": "earlier_closed_form" }`, naming only an earlier `closed_form` query; closed-form, properties, and asymptotic consumers never accept that target. The named source is eligible only when its sole answer is proved (possibly under assumptions), carries checked closed-form evidence, and has exactly one candidate. A dependent inherits and deduplicates the source conditions, used assumptions, and relevant unsupported assumptions within public bounds; overflow is unresolved. If the source is unavailable, the dependent remains correlated, is `inapplicable`, has a null normalized target, and names the source conclusion in its blocker. There is no fallback to the submitted expression or equation RHS. Derived operands preserve their source provenance but never change submitted work, direct-work aggregation, or scenarios. Equation-targeted queries consume only supported local effective-domain facts and report those constraint uses separately; local facts never leak to another equation or an expression query. Queries do not execute in scenario contexts.

Accepted query shape is broader than bounded evaluator applicability. The shipped evaluators cover conservative rational equivalence; geometric-linear finite or convergent infinite closed forms; partial direct `closed_form` support for one finite-polynomial nested `Sum` tree under bounded arithmetic, with depth four, eight total sum nodes, degree eight in each active binder, and affine-integral ranges that are proved ordered or proved empty; supported rational sign, valid-domain, singularity, and monotonicity properties; supported rational limits; and bounded rational or linear-exponential asymptotics. The nested family runs innermost-first behind checked antidifference and inclusive-boundary verification. It does not implicitly feed direct properties, limits, or asymptotics, while a proved candidate may feed a later equivalence or limit only through an explicit derived target. Its informational candidate remains distinct from binder-correct submitted direct work, equation reuse, scenarios, and output multiplicity. Valid questions outside these families return localized `unresolved` or `inapplicable` answers rather than invented mathematics. Their blockers identify the failed supported family, structural or resource bound, ambiguous axis, or missing precondition and give a safe reformulation direction when one exists. Observed and configured values appear only when bounded inspection measured them; a recovery hint neither certifies equivalence nor promises broader evaluator support.

For example, this request asks for a closed form of a convergent geometric-linear tail under explicit assumptions:

```json
{
  "expression": "Sum((k + 1) * q**k, (k, p, oo))",
  "variables": {
    "p": {"domain": "nonnegative_integer"},
    "q": {"domain": "real"}
  },
  "assumptions": [
    {"name": "q_nonnegative", "relationship": "0 <= q"},
    {"name": "tail_ratio", "relationship": "q < 1"}
  ],
  "queries": [{"name": "tail", "kind": "closed_form"}]
}
```

Each answer reports `proved`, `proved_under_assumptions`, `disproved`, `unresolved`, or `inapplicable`, plus conditions, assumptions used, unsupported relevant assumptions, blockers, evidence, and informational derived candidates. Derived candidates never replace submitted operation counts or work. An infinite mathematical expression may have a qualified query answer while retaining no finite direct-work count.

## Diagnostics and non-goals

Request diagnostics provide a Python-owned message, identify a field path when available, and may include a source span or supported alternative. Correct the localized request from the available details rather than broadening the dialect. Query blockers and proof qualifications remain part of a valid query answer, not request-validation diagnostics or warnings to discard.

The implemented analyzer does not accept LaTeX input, infer formulas from source, evaluate represented values numerically, validate physics, profile implementations, predict runtime or hardware behavior, model dimensions or implicit vectors, differentiate, approximate numerically, prove arbitrary theorems, solve general systems, generate recurrences, or generate code.

## Broader product direction (not implemented)

Potential future work includes additional safe mathematical frontends, richer expression constructs, scenario-context questions, dimensions, recurrence analysis, broader checked optimization families, and formula-to-code workflows. This direction is not accepted input or current agent guidance. New capabilities require explicit contracts, bounded semantics, qualification rules, tests, and documentation before callers may rely on them.
